allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 6 m up its host at 8 years and 12 m at 15. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: dark glossy green leaves, black berries.

appearance.organs.fruit.shape.kind.note: How PlantGen lays out an inflorescence, a choice of the model's (spec rework L1): the inflorescence characters set the cluster of any look a taxon draws as one (`"inflorescence": {}`), its kind, how many units it bears on each axis, its primary branches and how it holds itself. Sizes, stalks and spacing stay set by hand until programs size their organs from characters.

appearance.organs.leaf.note: FEIS (Waggy 2010, read): leaves 3 to 5 lobed in the juvenile phase and broadly lanceolate and unlobed in the adult phase, whose stems flower; other floras call the adult leaf ovate, rhombic or elliptic (search results only, the pages themselves were not read). So the leaf's own look is the adult's, an entire ovate blade, and its juvenile family the five-lobed palmate look, drawn on juvenile shoots (spec rework P6). The adult blade is drawn broadly ovate so that both draw about the leaf area the plant shades with: no source read gives the two phases' sizes apart.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an evergreen woody vine that climbs by clinging roots up trunks into the crowns of trees, with glossy, dark, three- to five-lobed leaves on climbing shoots and flowering, black-berried shoots where it reaches the light; introduced and invasive in the forests of the Pacific Northwest, where it smothers bigleaf maples. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.adult_age.note: The juvenile period is the time from germination to the first flowers, cones or seed, which the Woody Plant Seed Manual's tables give as the minimum seed-bearing age (spec rework P6). adult_age is the first year a program measuring it by the plant's age lets the plant flower or bear cones, so it is the juvenile period itself.

generator.params.adult_light.note: FEIS (Waggy 2010, read): adult ivy flowers in bright light, sexual reproduction typically occurs in climbing plants that reach sufficient light, and plants in the adult phase occur in the sun. So under climber revision 3 (spec rework P6) a side shoot of a climbing stem whose tip has at least this share of the open sky turns adult once the vine is past its juvenile period, as do free shoots; the share, 0.6, is hand-set so that only the brightest shoots turn adult (the growth model takes 0.35 for full sun on a leaf).

generator.params.adult_rise.note: FEIS (Waggy 2010, read), after Stein and Fosket (1969): an adult shoot grows upright (orthotropic) and has no aerial roots, where a juvenile shoot creeps or climbs (plagiotropic) on them. So under climber revision 3 (spec rework P6) an adult shoot no longer clings or seeks its host and rises under a tropism of its own; its elasticity, 0.25, a little below a clinging shoot's climb, is hand-set.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant bears both sexes, unless its taxa state it dioecious.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the climber base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the climber program gave as defaults until then.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

host.note: The host the spec's authors chose for this guest, grown at the age, environment and seed given.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy (plant forms milestone F7). Calibration against measurements and photographs comes later.
